## Purpose and status

Agreed on 23 September 2026. This case provides the common wind-farm and
onshore hydrogen-delivery basis for the centralised and turbine-level
comparisons. It is an idealised case based on IJmuiden Ver Beta, not a claim to
reproduce the developer's final design.

The authoritative article inputs are in
[reference_case.toml](scenarios/reference_case.toml). Values displayed here are
loaded from that record; dimensions and spacing are calculated by
[the reference-case calculation](analysis/reference_case.py). These are case
choices, not defaults for the component methodology. Both architecture
templates include the same generated common case (see
[Common operating case](#sec-common-operating-case)); this note does not claim
a completed production or cost run. Remaining preparation is tracked in
[O1](OPEN_POINTS.md).

## Common inputs and their basis

Identifies the geographical reference; it does not identify the supplied DOWA extraction point. |

The installed wind capacity is derived, not independently prescribed:

$$
P_{\mathrm{farm}}=N P_r.
$$

Here $P_{\mathrm{farm}}$ is in MW, $N$ is a turbine count and $P_r$ is in
MW/turbine. The result is **{{< var ijv-installed-mw >}} MW**. “Approximately
2 GW” is a descriptive label; calculations retain the exact count-times-rating
result without introducing an electricity-grid export cap.

## Layout and spacing derived from area

Let $B$ be crosswind breadth and $L$ along-wind length, both in km. With
$A$ in km² and dimensionless $r=B/L$:

$$
B=\sqrt{Ar},\qquad L=\sqrt{A/r},\qquad BL=A.
$$

This gives **{{< var ijv-breadth-km >}} km across the wind** and
**{{< var ijv-length-km >}} km along the wind**. The adopted regular-grid
construction chooses the number of crosswind columns $n_B$ and along-wind rows
$n_L$ as:

$$
n_B=\left\lceil\sqrt{Nr}\right\rceil,\qquad
n_L=\left\lceil N/n_B\right\rceil.
$$

The resulting grid has {{< var ijv-columns >}} columns and
{{< var ijv-rows >}} rows: {{< var ijv-full-rows >}} full rows and a centred
final row of {{< var ijv-last-row >}} turbines. This row convention is an
explicit modelling choice; area and aspect ratio alone do not uniquely define
a turbine layout.

Turbine centres span the equivalent rectangle, with no additional boundary
setback. Consequently, the separations in metres are:

$$
d_B=\frac{1000B}{n_B-1},\qquad
d_L=\frac{1000L}{n_L-1}.
$$

The factor 1000 converts km to m. Crosswind spacing is
**{{< var ijv-spacing-crosswind-m >}} m** and along-wind spacing is
**{{< var ijv-spacing-alongwind-m >}} m**. The shorter final row retains $d_B$
and is centred within the same breadth. All wake and collection calculations
must use the resulting common turbine coordinates, rather than a separate
area-based spacing proxy.

Replacing the net site by a rectangle deliberately omits its actual shape,
internal corridors and exclusions. This is a comparative layout, not a
demonstration of site-permit compliance. Detailed polygon checks remain D7.

## Wind record and orientation

Use the supplied DOWA-derived hourly workbook and fitted sector table already
described on [Wind Resource and Weibull Distribution](../../wind_resource_and_layout/wind_resource_and_weibull.qmd).
Their paths are recorded in the case file. DOWA is the underlying atlas
[@dutchOffshoreWindAtlas]; the atlas citation does not independently establish
the workbook's extraction point or height. Retain the page's existing metadata
and period limitations without substituting an unrelated wind record.

The adopted orientation follows the centre of the most frequent direction
sector in the supplied table: **{{< var ijv-dominant-from-deg >}}°**, interpreted
as the meteorological direction **from** which wind arrives, clockwise from
north. Thus the short axis runs southwest–northeast and the long axis
northwest–southeast. Sector labels in the existing file are lower bin edges;
use bin centres when preparing wake states. The centre is calculated from the
stored sector spacing rather than entered as another independent case value.

This documents the adopted interpretation. It does not recover the missing
direction-convention metadata for the original extraction. Both architectures
must receive identical annual wind-state weights and turbine-level generation
before architecture-specific losses.

## Common operating case {#sec-common-operating-case}

[`prepare_common_case.py`](analysis/prepare_common_case.py) turns this record
into `scenarios/common_case.toml` and the data files in `scenarios/common/`.
Both architecture templates include that file. The model rejects any key defined
in both a template and the included file, so the templates cannot silently depart
from the common case. The script requires the optional PyWake dependency; the
generated files are committed so that running a case does not.

**Coordinates.** Positions are in metres with $x$ east, $y$ north and the
origin at the farm centre. With the dominant direction $\theta$ (wind **from**,
clockwise from north), the downwind and crosswind unit vectors are

$$
\mathbf{e}_d=(-\sin\theta,\,-\cos\theta),\qquad
\mathbf{e}_c=(\cos\theta,\,-\sin\theta).
$$

A turbine in row $i$ at crosswind offset $u$ is placed at
$u\,\mathbf{e}_c+\left(i-\tfrac{n_L-1}{2}\right)d_L\,\mathbf{e}_d$, with
$u$ centred within its row. Turbines are numbered row by row from the upwind
edge. The centralised AC strings follow this order, which is provisional until
the platform location is set (O3/O7).

**Turbine curve.** The tabulated electrical power and thrust coefficient come
from the release's rotor-performance table, pinned by commit and checksum in the
record. The table's power column is electrical output: its power coefficient is
the aerodynamic coefficient times the 95.7% generator efficiency. This matches
the model's common generator-output boundary. Solver noise of up to 0.06 kW
above rating is capped at the 15 MW rating. Zero power and thrust are declared
just outside the 3–25 m/s operating range, because PyWake would otherwise hold
the first tabulated value for waked turbines below cut-in; idle-rotor thrust is
neglected.

The adopted [turbine electrical boundary](../../turbine_system/power_electronics.qmd)
is now inverter AC output, before the transformer. The source-table description
above records the existing data provenance, not a verified conversion to that
boundary. **TODO (O2):** confirm which converter losses the table includes or
document its conversion before recovering inverter losses for decentralised
hydrogen. Existing operating states have not been relabelled or rescaled.

**Operating states.** The fitted sector table is converted to one joint table of
direction and speed states. Direction is spread uniformly within each 30° sector
in {{< var ijv-direction-step-deg >}}° steps, and speed is binned in
{{< var ijv-speed-bin-m-s >}} m/s steps represented by bin midpoints between cut-in
and cut-out. Weights are the Weibull probabilities times the central annual
hours; the {{< var ijv-no-power-hours >}} h/year below cut-in or above cut-out form
one zero-power state. This gives {{< var ijv-state-count >}} states, including that
state. The hourly speeds are treated as hub-height speeds, because the workbook
does not record its extraction height. This is an explicit assumption carried over
from the legacy model, not a height correction.

PyWake {{< var ijv-pywake-version >}} evaluates every state with the model's wake
configuration and the central turbulence intensity
{{< var wind-turbulence-intensity >}}. The resulting table gives wake-affected
power for each turbine at the generator output, before any architecture-specific
loss. A zero-hour design state, `design-all-rated`, sets every turbine at rated
power as the common peak-duty basis. The annual states reach this full-farm
output at high wind speeds, so it is an attained operating condition rather than
an added margin.

| Result (before availability and architecture losses) | Value |
|---|---:|
| No-wake annual energy | {{< var ijv-no-wake-aep-gwh >}} GWh |
| Wake-affected annual energy | {{< var ijv-wake-aep-gwh >}} GWh |
| Wake loss | {{< var ijv-wake-loss >}} |
| Wake-affected gross capacity factor | {{< var ijv-gross-capacity-factor >}} |

: Common operating case generated from the record.

Two checks bound the discretisation. Single-turbine energy from the fitted
Weibull states differs from energy from the {{< var ijv-hourly-record-count >}}
hourly records by {{< var ijv-weibull-vs-hourly-difference >}}. Wake-affected
energy with the adopted direction step differs from a 1° calculation by
{{< var ijv-direction-step-difference >}}. Neither check validates the wake model:
turbulence intensity remains a provisional legacy value, blockage is excluded,
and the wake formulation has not been benchmarked
([Wake Modelling and Spacing](../../wind_resource_and_layout/wake_modelling_and_spacing.qmd)).

## Export and onshore delivery boundary

The reported product is hydrogen delivered at the common onshore receipt
interface at the adopted pressure. Include the export pipeline, landfall and
receipt functions needed to reach that boundary; exclude subsequent backbone
transport, storage, distribution and end use. The receipt equipment scope and
its supply, installation and operating costs remain O9.

The agreed export length is a scenario assumption. For context, the published
Beta electricity-connection assessment gives a **146 km offshore cable route**
toward Maasvlakte [@ijmuidenBeta2021ExportMER, Table 2-14, p. 67]. This is route
evidence for a different carrier, not an adopted hydrogen-pipeline length.
A particular landfall and engineered route remain unresolved.

The West-Netherlands hydrogen-network document describes initial operation at
**30–50 bar** and possible future operation up to **66 bar**
[@hynetwork2026WestNRD, p. 18]. Those are source-reported network conditions;
the article deliberately adopts the upper level as its delivery requirement.
It does not claim that every connection currently requires that pressure.

Compression and pipeline equations use **absolute** pressure. The agreed
delivery and stack outlet pressures are gauge values and are converted once, at
the model boundary:

$$
p_{\mathrm{abs}}=p_{\mathrm{g}}+p_{\mathrm{atm}}.
$$

All pressures in this equation are in bar. The atmospheric basis
$p_{\mathrm{atm}}$ is the standard atmosphere,
{{< var standard-atmospheric-pressure >}} (exactly 101 325 Pa
[@nist2008SP811]), applied at both the offshore stack outlet and the onshore
receipt boundary. This is an explicit modelling assumption: both points are
near sea level, and weather-driven barometric variation, of the order of a few
hundredths of a bar, is not modelled.

The result is a delivery pressure of
**{{< var ijv-delivery-pressure-bar-a >}} bar(a)** and a stack outlet pressure
of **{{< var ijv-stack-outlet-pressure-bar-a >}} bar(a)**, calculated by
[the reference-case calculation](analysis/reference_case.py). Scenario inputs
take these absolute values; the gauge values are never copied into an
absolute-pressure field. Any pressure loss through
receipt equipment belongs upstream of the delivery interface and must be
accounted for explicitly rather than hidden in a pressure margin.

## Stack sizing and comparison cases

Define the dimensionless overplant factor as:

$$
f=\frac{P_{\mathrm{stack,requested}}}{P_{\mathrm{wind,served}}},
$$

where both capacities are in MW at their stated rating boundaries. Central
stacks serve the complete farm; each turbine-level package serves its turbine.
Actual installed stack capacity follows the model's integer module sizing.
Overplanting changes stack capacity; it does not automatically increase the
wind rating or BOP design capacity. Operation must still cover auxiliary loads
within available wind power.

Start both architectures at the agreed baseline factor. Retain the agreed
upper factor for deferred sensitivity work (D6), not as a demonstrated feasible
design or an optimised result. Preserve the article's centralised, conservative
turbine-level and converter-reduced comparison cases; electrical equipment and
efficiency choices remain O2.

## Pressure and export-diameter design grid

The article design grid, agreed on 1 October 2026, evaluates compressor
discharge pressures of **50–150 bar(g) in 10 bar steps** and export-pipe
**internal diameters of 4–8 inches in 0.5 inch steps**. These are scenario
choices, not supplier qualification limits or a selected baseline. The
[grid record](scenarios/pressure_diameter_grid.toml) is authoritative: its
11 pressures and 9 diameters give **99 combinations per architecture**.

The [design-case runner](analysis/run_design_cases.py) expands that record.
It adds the central standard atmospheric pressure to each gauge pressure and
multiplies each diameter in inches by the exact conversion **0.0254 m/inch**.
The resulting absolute pressures and internal diameters feed the existing
compression and pipeline calculations; they are recorded in each run's
`design_cases.csv` and case results.

The 50 and 60 bar(g) cases cannot supply the agreed 66 bar(g) delivery boundary
without intermediate recompression, which is outside this design. They remain
in the comparison as **infeasible**. Higher pressures pass only this initial
boundary check; they are not thereby proven feasible. Pipe capacity and integer
parallel-pipe count must still be checked against calculated production.

For central production, compressor discharge is the export inlet. For
turbine-level production, collection losses intervene: section diameters and
inlet/outlet pressures must support a separately declared export inlet pressure.
The grid does not impose its export diameter on collection sections or assume
zero collection pressure loss. These section choices remain O7. Cases lacking
required inputs report **not_parameterized**, without selecting a baseline or
claiming a complete cost comparison. O3 platform sizing still requires the
complete topside mass, fabrication rates, yard integration and installation basis.

For example, from the repository root:

```powershell
uv run python research_articles/turbine_level_hydrogen/analysis/run_design_cases.py research_articles/turbine_level_hydrogen/scenarios/centralised.toml research_articles/turbine_level_hydrogen/scenarios/pressure_diameter_grid.toml --output model_runs/central-pressure-diameter
```

Use the decentralised template and a separate output directory for the
turbine-level case. Each output directory must be new; results remain local.

## First-article installation choice

Both architectures select the [fixed normal-turbine installation reference](../../offshore_installation/turbine_and_foundation_installation.qmd#sec-article-installation-reference)
through the shared scenario: **{{< var installation-reference-eur2025-per-turbine >}}
EUR2025/turbine**, without a mass discount. This replaces only turbine installation;
foundation installation retains the existing common campaign method and its
unresolved inputs. The original turbine campaign model and data remain available.
Hydrogen-equipment installation and commissioning are assumed comparable to the
work for removed power electronics, so no separate installation charge is added.
This is an article modelling assumption, not sourced proof of equal work.
No new equipment mass or largest-lift input is adopted. Central-platform
installation remains within EPCI.

## Remaining preparation

**O1 is partially resolved.** The site, count/rating, area, schematic geometry,
representative depth, wind-data basis, export distance, delivery-pressure
and stack-outlet pressure interpretations and overplanting range are agreed. Before claiming executable
common-case results:

- The common coordinates, turbine definition, operating and peak-duty states,
  and converted pressures are connected to both templates (above).
- Complete the remaining design inputs needed by the selected branches:
  collection section pressures/diameters and distributed export inlet (O7), complete topside mass and installation basis
  (O3), and electrical interface inputs (O2). Collection origins and network design are
  linked to O3/O7; onshore receipt details remain O9.
